domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers fundamental business and law principles required for successfully managing a commercial contracting enterprise within the regulatory framework established by the governing authorities and participating state boards.

This domain focuses upon detailed project management practices for overseeing construction operations, coordinating jobsite schedules, managing subcontractors, and ensuring that commercial building projects are completed efficiently according to plans.

This domain addresses thorough estimating and bidding techniques for commercial construction projects, teaching candidates how to perform accurate quantity takeoffs, calculate material expenses, and prepare competitive bids for clients.

This domain presents building codes and regulations governing commercial structures, ensuring that contractors understand structural requirements, zoning laws, and administrative procedures necessary for proper building compliance and safety.

This domain outlines construction materials and methods used in building projects, exploring the physical properties of concrete, steel, wood, and other commercial building components alongside correct installation procedures.

This domain details important safety standards and OSHA requirements for construction sites, focusing on hazard recognition, personal protective equipment, fall protection, and maintaining a secure working environment for all personnel.

This domain examines contract law principles relevant to construction agreements, detailing how to establish binding terms, interpret project specifications, manage legal liabilities, and resolve disputes professionally between involved parties.

This domain explores financial management practices for construction businesses, teaching candidates how to implement proper accounting principles, track project costs, handle cash flow management, and establish accurate budgets.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive at the computer-based testing center early with proper identification. Manage your time carefully across the 100 questions during the 180 minutes allowed to ensure successful completion.

faq.answer_text: The exam consists of exactly 100 multiple-choice questions administered in a secure, computer-based format at authorized PSI testing centers nationwide for all registered candidates seeking their professional contractor license.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: The standard passing score requirement is set at 70 percentage, though specific state licensing boards may enforce their own unique regulatory guidelines for all participating exam applicants.
You are given a total of 180 minutes to complete all questions within the computer-based testing environment at a designated PSI location during your scheduled appointment time.
The official exam registration price is established at 90.0 USD, which must be paid directly when scheduling your test appointment at the center to secure your testing slot.
faq.question_title: What is the cost of the exam?

editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the NASCLA Accredited General Contractor Commercial Exam. Understand business law, project management, estimating, codes, safety, and more.

methodology.summary: This informative page was constructed carefully using official NASCLA study documentation and standard regulatory source materials to ensure complete factual accuracy and reliability.

editorial.overview: The NASCLA Accredited General Contractor Commercial Exam is a thorough certification testing professional knowledge across eight distinct domains. Candidates must master business and law, project management, estimating and bidding, building codes and regulations, construction materials and methods, safety, contract law, and financial management to successfully earn their commercial contractor licensure across participating state jurisdictions.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review all official NASCLA study documentation and reference materials in great depth to ensure complete familiarity with every tested concept across all available subjects. Focus your thorough preparation on the eight tested domains, paying close attention to building codes, safety regulations, financial accounting principles, and contract law requirements.
editorial.who_should_take: General contractors and commercial construction professionals who are seeking professional licensure across multiple participating jurisdictions should take this detailed examination to demonstrate their technical competence.

exam_name: NASCLA Accredited General Contractor Commercial Exam
exam_rules: Exams administered at PSI testing centers. No personal reference materials permitted unless otherwise specified for your state exam. Some states allow open-book exams with approved code books — verify your state's rules. Calculator may be permitted; check candidate handbook for your specific exam. State contractor license requirements vary — NASCLA accreditation provides reciprocity in participating states.
id_requirements: Government-issued photo ID required at PSI testing center. Name on ID must match registration exactly.

official_study_resources.notes: Official NASCLA reference book used as the basis for the accredited exams. Available through NASCLA; widely used as a study guide and allowed as a reference on the exam in some states.
official_study_resources.title: NASCLA Contractor's Guide to Business, Law, and Project Management

official_study_resources.notes: PSI provides candidate handbooks for each state/exam combination at no charge.
official_study_resources.title: PSI Candidate Handbook and Practice Materials

passing_score_scale: Percentage (70% passing for most contractor exams; varies by state)
renewal_options: Most state contractor licenses expire every 2 years. Renewal typically requires continuing education (number of hours varies by state) and payment of renewal fees to the state licensing board. NASCLA accreditation does not expire, but state licenses must be maintained separately.

retake_policy.notes: Retake policies vary by state licensing board and PSI exam rules. Check your state contractor licensing board and PSI candidate handbook for applicable waiting periods, attempt limits, and retake fees.

testing_centers.notes: NASCLA accredited exams and state contractor license exams administered by PSI Exams at PSI testing centers nationwide. Schedule online at candidate.psiexams.com.
